requirements: systemd with nss-systemd for passwd and group (sessions' users are boot-local /run/userdb records)

One image coding uid/gid, >=1000 and below 200000, with no privileged groups: only sessions whose NAS volume predates member machines run as it; every other session runs as its own uid/gid in 200000-524287, registered per boot
coding-user-owned isolated repository workspace per session

Each attached session's NAS data volume at /workspace/<workerId> and separate protected NAS custody volume at /var/lib/qorpera-coding/<workerId>, hot-plugged over virtiofs; no local directory fallback

resourceProfile names only the log bound (maxLogBytes): a command has no time, memory, CPU or task limit of its own; sessions share the machine by equal cgroup weights, and qorpera-coding.slice keeps MemoryMax=90% so the guest's own control (lxd-agent, systemd, the watchdog) always has memory
Pinned Node/Python/native toolchain and browser dependencies selected in the signed image recipe

No self-update: apt-daily.timer, apt-daily-upgrade.timer, apt-daily.service, apt-daily-upgrade.service and unattended-upgrades.service masked (links from /etc/systemd/system to /dev/null); every storage-checked action refuses otherwise with RUNNER_IMAGE_SELF_UPDATE_ENABLED
credentialPolicy: No provider, GitHub, cloud-control, member or office credentials enter the command environment or coding user home.
provisioningOrder: Install and verify pinned OS/runtime/toolchains in image build, never from model/root command; mask the five apt self-update units

Install helper artifacts and systemd units with reviewed manifest digest; create root-owned0755 /workspace, /var/lib/qorpera-coding and /run/qorpera-coding in image; do not enable ordinary coding admission
Per session, while its turn runs: hot-plug its exact admitted NAS data and custody devices and wait until both are mounted
prepare <workerId>: create the session's root-owned boot-local runtime and configuration folders
install <workerId>: publish root-owned0444 guest/storage configuration bound to current volume generation and boot
initialize <workerId>: verify mounts and markers, register the session's user, then initialize its uid-owned data directories and root-protected custody only on verified mounts
Enable watchdog timer, refresh authorized queue lease, then admit commands
At the end of the turn, detach <workerId>: stop and see stopped the session's slice, sync, remove its boot-local state and user; then unplug its devices
